chapitres.competenceChapitre: Explorer le rôle de l'individu dans la société, en se concentrant sur les devoirs civiques, les problèmes sociaux et l'identité culturelle.

objectifsLesson.description: Read a text about a social issue (e.g., female mutilation) and be able to identify the perpetrators and the reasons behind the act.
Vocabulary: Social issues (e.g., female mutilation, perpetrators, abuse of rights).
Grammar: Using relative pronouns (who, which, that) to define and describe.
Listen to instructions for obtaining an official document (e.g., a passport) and correctly fill out a sample application form.
Vocabulary: Administrative terms (e.g., application form, fee, birth certificate, submit).
Grammar: Forming questions with modals (can, could, may) to ask for information politely.
Read a text about the challenges of the educational system and discuss its relevance to students' lives and future.
Vocabulary: Education (e.g., certificate, qualification, relevant, curriculum).
Grammar: Using the passive voice to focus on the action rather than the doer (e.g., 'The educational system was questioned.')

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Comprendre le monde du travail, postuler à un emploi et valoriser le volontariat.

objectifsLesson.description: Simulate a job interview, learning to introduce oneself, discuss qualifications, and answer common interview questions.
Vocabulary: Job application (e.g., interview, CV, qualifications, experience, skills).
Grammar: Using the present perfect tense to talk about experiences ('I have applied for several jobs.')
Analyze a job advertisement and write a simple but structured cover letter in response.
Vocabulary: Job advertisement (e.g., position, requirements, salary, apply).
Grammar: Using modals of advice (should) and obligation (have to).
Read about the benefits of volunteering and discuss its importance for personal growth and community development.
Vocabulary: Community service (e.g., volunteer, community, benefits, skills, experience).
Grammar: Expressing purpose with to + infinitive and in order to.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Examiner la relation entre les individus, leur santé et leur environnement, en mettant l'accent sur la prévention.

objectifsLesson.description: Simulate a doctor-patient conversation to give and receive advice on health issues, using appropriate vocabulary.
Vocabulary: Health and illness (e.g., symptoms, temperature, prescription, auto-medication).
Grammar: Using modals for advice (should, shouldn't, must, have to).
Read a medical brochure or a text on disease prevention (e.g., COVID-19) and write a list of health tips for a school magazine.
Vocabulary: Prevention (e.g., vaccine, protection, hygiene, symptoms, treatment).
Grammar: Using conditional sentences (Type 1) to talk about real possibilities ('If you take the vaccine, you are better protected.')

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Prendre conscience des problèmes environnementaux et proposer des solutions écologiques.

objectifsLesson.description: Read a text about waste management problems in urban areas and discuss the causes and effects.
Vocabulary: Environment (e.g., rubbish disposal, waste, toxic, recycle, contaminate).
Grammar: Using the causative have (get) to talk about services ('We should have our garbage collected regularly.')
Listen to a report on an ecological initiative (e.g., recycling) and write a list of simple eco-friendly tips for the community.
Vocabulary: Recycling (e.g., recycle, reduce, reuse, waste, environment).
Grammar: Using the gerund as a subject ('Recycling helps preserve the environment.')
Read a text explaining the process of erosion and discuss the consequences and possible solutions to protect the land.
Vocabulary: Geography/Conservation (e.g., erosion, sediment, topsoil, conservation, windbreaks).
Grammar: Using the present continuous tense to describe ongoing processes ('Soil is eroding faster than it is being formed.')

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Explorer les dynamiques de la vie moderne : technologie, médias et communication à l'ère numérique.

objectifsLesson.description: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of social media and write a formal email of complaint about a faulty online purchase.
Vocabulary: Technology (e.g., social media, applications, online, account, hacked).
Grammar: Using the past perfect to describe an action that happened before another in the past ('He hadn't known that online shopping was cheaper, so he bought from a supermarket.')
Read a user manual or listen to an automated telephone message to understand options and follow instructions correctly.
Vocabulary: Customer service (e.g., refund, warranty, complaint, customer service, option).
Grammar: Using reported speech to relay information ('The Mayor announced that they would be sorting out their garbage.')

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Réfléchir aux choix personnels, à l'identité, à l'émigration et aux problèmes sociaux dans un monde globalisé.

objectifsLesson.description: Write a letter to a family member to explain a personal choice (e.g., career path) and persuade them of its merits.
Vocabulary: Career (e.g., profession, journalist, doctor, opportunities, society).
Grammar: Using future tenses (will, be going to) to express intentions and predictions.
Read a text about the desire to travel abroad and discuss the concept of 'home' and the reasons for or against emigration.
Vocabulary: Emigration (e.g., abroad, emigrate, opportunities, home, identity).
Grammar: Using modals of speculation (may, might, could) to discuss possibilities.
Write a speech as a senior prefect to address a school issue (e.g., drug consumption, violence), giving causes, consequences, and solutions.
Vocabulary: Social issues (e.g., violence, drug consumption, consequences, prevention, awareness).
Grammar: Using linking words (because, therefore, however, although) to structure a coherent argument.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: Consolider les acquis et évaluer les compétences en vue de l'examen final.

objectifsLesson.description: Review the main vocabulary themes (social issues, health, environment, technology) and key grammar points (passive voice, reported speech, conditionals, modals) covered during the year.
Assess acquired skills through a comprehensive test mirroring the exam format: grammar, vocabulary, reading comprehension, and composition writing.
Analyze assessment errors, provide feedback, and consolidate weak points to ensure mastery of key concepts.
